key_insight: Use ensemble covariance from a nudged coarse simulator as a Jacobian-free proxy for local instability geometry, then condition a small FiLM module to improve rare-event emulation from limited data.
engineering_relevance: This offers a non-intrusive way to boost surrogate models for extreme-event prediction without changing the underlying simulator, which is valuable when training data are scarce and tail accuracy matters.
method: Run a nudged coarse ensemble around a synchronized trajectory to extract covariance-based instability features.
Inject those geometry statistics through a lightweight FiLM conditioner into an unchanged prediction backbone.
Tested with a Transformer-style corrector on a low-dimensional chaotic system and a STORN corrector on quasi-geostrophic flow.
evidence_signal: The conditioned models improved 99th-percentile exceedance errors in the chaotic benchmark and, in QG flow, reduced tail, exceedance-frequency, and exceedance-area errors using only 50 time units, even outperforming a baseline trained with 20 times more high-resolution data on averaged high-threshold diagnostics.
watch_item: The approach depends on a meaningful synchronization/ensemble setup and may be sensitive to noise level, ensemble size, and how well covariance captures the relevant instability geometry.
paper_title: Mechanism-Aware Ensemble Conditioning for Data-Limited Emulation of Extreme Events
